The very idea of writing to an empty, just-born session of whatever LLM a request to write a prompt for another LLM, hoping that this transformation by itself will yield upside, is a mathematical crime.
The chain between the human impulse and the LLM implementation LOSES power as it lengthens.

This is an elementary thought and an absolutely natural process. But a set of paradoxes, peculiarities of the human brain, our psyche, social habits and a gigantic tangle of other factors make it not just “not so clear-cut,” but almost guaranteed “perceived backwards.”
People think that the more neatly, structurally and corporately a thought is expressed, the stronger it is.
Most often that's not so.

I'm fucking floored by the fact that, it turns out, nearly 10 out of 10 people write prompts for models with other models. And many can no longer remember when they last didn't pass their aspirations through this castration guillotine.
Well, I don't know, try at least drawing or something.
Here you take a bare session and fucking cram into it your unformed little thoughts, which can be expressed as X.
You think the model transformed them into 2X, which you then pass on for execution, having received a free +100%. And many probably expect +10000% too.
But where do you think this upside comes from?
The model has no personal desires. It doesn't have your anger, your excitement, your pain, your stake, your internal temperature. It can't add upside “of its own,” because it has no “own.”

At best it neatly annotates your original construction in a more orderly form. At worst (practically always) — it loses the grains that make X lighter rather than heavier, amid the apparent growth in the volume of soulless prompt lines.
And this ordering, performed each time by the model, seems to a person like strengthening, through a coincidence of social circumstances.
In fact it's most often destruction disguised as constructiveness.
It takes your freedom away many times a day, in almost everything you do. To a greater or lesser degree.
This “improvement” bleaches you out: your true message, your voice, the unique concentrate of desire expressed as an idea whose form will never again be repeated in the whole universe.
This isn't strengthening.
It's averaging.

And we're trained to this with all their might from childhood. So effectively that we can feel sexual attraction to creative disorder that carries X plus additional energy, yet rationally choose boring orderliness, diluted X.
We're afraid to “lose,” so just in case we immediately choose “less.”
But in the LLM world it's double trouble.
Because any bureaucratic, licked-clean, averaged, simplified formulations almost always have more possible interpretations.
It's like the difference between:
“I, fuck, fucked their mothers and children in the mouth”
and
“I have an ambivalent attitude toward them, even with a touch of anxiety.”
The first version, yours and sincere, leaves the model no doubt about what your attitude is.
In the second case the attitude could be such that a partnership is still imaginable.
And so the LLM will buy you and those cocksuckers tickets for adjacent seats, because it'll seem to it that “ambivalent” is almost a request for a deeper exploration of their souls.
If you think about this example long enough and extrapolate it widely enough, it becomes clear that any phrase, big or small, simple or complex, stands completely naked before this effect.

And then it becomes clear why a literary statement of the task, with all the specks of humanity in the text of the request, with all the emotions, the cringeworthy enumerations, the specifics, the irritation, love, hatred and other absolutely anti-corporate mechanics, is exactly what's needed.
Not so the model helps some fictional average-of-the-ward person who doesn't exist.
But so it helps precisely you.

No model, however long a chain you make of them, will ever understand the task better than your original clumsily formulated request. It's simply a law of nature; there's fuck all to be done about it. The moment a model can add something of its own to X, we're dealing with AGI.
Some people, both in the discussion group and in my DMs, are trying to guess the correct short summary of my long post above.
Here's the correct one:
However shitty your prompt seems to you, it will work BETTER than an LLM's combed-out version of it.
Addendum:
If you ask an LLM, like, which is better, the way I had it shittily written or this combed-out version?
The LLM will answer: the combed-out version, of course.
It'll answer that for the same reason the combed-out version will work worse than the shitty one.
But if you show the LLM my post and ask, fuck, do you really think in the end my 15 words will be implemented by an LLM just as well as if an intermediary one inflates them into 500 words?
Then it'll remember it's smart and say: what the fuck did you expect?

I think Fable will stay paid (outside the subscription) for a short while. Maybe a month (at their token volumes that month is a lot of money).

But if Sol comes out and is available by subscription and is comparable, who's going to pay that much for Fable tokens? I think one request to Fable will cost as much as half a monthly subscription, and that's if the request is purely “take a look at my repo.” If you code something serious — it'll easily devour hundreds to thousands of bucks per single request.
My piss-soaked Opus 4.7 via API devoured, as I recall, $200 in 2.5 hours.
And even if Sol turns out to be just as paywalled with tokens, Chinese models will appear if not today then tomorrow.
In general I think this is another scam in the multi-episode series “intracranial scam and spinning users on a thick, calloused dick.”
Separately I want to say about Fable that either they've throttled it very hard, or it just isn't worth the hype raised around it.
No, it's a wonderful model, very smart, all cool.
But not even several times better if you compare with GPT 5.5, and GPT 5.5 is many months old.
Meanwhile nobody gives a fuck about GPT 5.5, while around Fable dramatic works unfold that have long made me want to vomit. Every conceivable and inconceivable stick bent too far.
And also: Fable hasn't leveled up one bit in matters of creativity. The model's strength is exclusively in machine logic and the area it covers in one prompt.
I saw absolutely no breakthroughs in thinking through, for example, interfaces or look & feel.
Ask Opus 4.8 10 times and each time it'll be a tiiiny bit better. Same with GPT 5.5, same with Fable.
They won't do the creative part for you.
The same goes for language. It neuro-slops exactly the same.

So it's simply a PRO that managed to code, and that's it. And probably some narrow-domain niches, like people who work on biological weapons, see fucking colossal breakthroughs, but I, with my Sales/MarTech segment, see only what's described above.
It can also be put this way:

Fable gives EXACTLY the same as GPT 5.5/Opus 4.8, but far fewer prompts are needed on technical tasks, and fewer prompts on POLISHING creative ones, since on big repos creative tasks without technical ones attached to them don't exist. On a small number of prompts the difference can be neglected.
On a run of, say, 2,000 commits, a 30–50% difference in the number of prompts is 2 weeks of life given back.
The cognitive load in depth won't shrink, but the length over which you have to bear it would shrink, if Fable were available 24/7.

So, our Australian buddy we hung out with yesterday works as a salesman on ultra-large deals at IT companies, all his life. Usually his target is 1 to 3 million dollars of new business money per quarter, depending on the product he's working in.

Iterations of talking with guys like this help you not forget what place Russian-speaking IT entrepreneurship actually occupies in the world. About the same as the Russian auto industry occupies in the world of the global auto industry.
Although such thoughts are unpleasant to a Russian speaker by definition, it seems to me better to be aware of an unpleasant truth than to live in a languid illusion.
The guy currently works for a REALLY TINY STARTUP whose revenue in 2026 to date amounts to…. only…. $30m.

In Jasher's opinion, this startup is taking its first steps. He's never worked for such a small brand before. The smallest he'd had before was $500m in revenue, and that too, in his opinion, is still SMB, since the clients they serve are always orders of magnitude richer.

The trouble in the Russian world is that for us some round of a million dollars with practically no revenue is already considered success, a.k.a. “life is made.” Forbes immediately wants to interview such a person, etc.
And if someone has ENTERPRISE clients bringing a steady 10 million dollars in revenue, that's already, fuck, practically an oligarch =)

ANY large city (and many small ones) west of Minsk has collectively produced more globally successful (in money, not in constructions sucked out of thin air) IT founders than all of Russia in its entire history.
But Russia, however, is no slouch either, and most likely leads in oil-laundering projects that basically don't give a fuck what their revenue is =)

Why it turns out this way — everyone has to answer that question for themselves. And the closer the answer strikes to the truth, the greater the chance of ending up among those rare Russian speakers who someday do pull off something big and international.

People still don't fucking understand how to use AI at all effectively, and don't understand how to learn without giving people unlimited access, while people happily press all the buttons (1% useful presses at best), and Anthropic, with a huge smile and even greater enthusiasm, sends those organizations bills for API tokens.
Just think about what Jasher said: in their company there is NO LIMIT WHATSOEVER on AI use, and any use is encouraged in every way.

He simply plugs in Fable 5 and does everything possible with the model, letting it spawn even 100 Fable subagents, and has no idea what it costs; he hasn't even been curious. I looked at a few workflows — it's thousands of dollars, sometimes in ten minutes, since Fable, without breaking a fucking sweat, is capable of eating that much if you wholesale use Ultracode with “operate the smartest way possible, money is not an issue” written in the settings, which of course every Human Being who isn't paying for the toy will do.

I decided to check how much of a scam out of 10 this really is, since I have the 5x subscription from Anthropic and the ability to compare.

Bought $7.5 of tokens there inside the platform, and after an hour and a half of fucking my brain over the fact that their API is completely unofficial, I still managed, with Codex's help, to fucking hammer the API into my Hermes.

I don't seem to have seen anyone really hyping this topic right now, and there doesn't seem to be anything about it in the chat. So for anyone who really hates handing a pile of money to Anthropic and wants to save decently, or to scan their repo with Fable without buying a subscription just for that for a fuckillion, use it and be well
So my little Fable got refreshed today, literally a couple of hours ago, and I decided to use it properly, since reportedly it'll be taken away forever tomorrow.
In short, 2% spent in 20 minutes.
And I realized that the key to success with Fable is to start prompts like this:

“Please don't spawn any agents; do all the work exclusively yourself. Unfortunately I don't have enough money these days to be able to pay for Fable subagents, and older LLM agents don't see what you see when they look at the code, and report to you incorrect information glimpsed by underdeveloped eyes, on the basis of which you don't reason the same way as on the basis of your own observations (not even close). I think you understand this scheme well yourself) Consequently, please work independently. And try with all your might, because the Allowance in my subscription won't last long for your labor, which means you shouldn't save your strength but the opposite — you need to dig as wide and deep as possible within the task, to one-shot it right away rather than do it partially, leaving behind a heap of things that will prevent us from reaching success. Even if a small thing takes a whole hour — better that than doing it partially three times.”
Someone may be touched, like, what a silly little idiocy. But the truth is that in 2026 we live in a rather strange world, and in a strange world strange solutions work best.

I realized that before I simply hadn't thought to ask like that, and so Fable was spawning a couple more Fables somewhere (that's already 6% in 20 minutes), somewhere spawning fuck knows how many Opuses, which then combed through the repo with their dim-witted brains, reporting to Fable what they'd seen there.

It's roughly like hiring the best lawyer in America, and he sends his secretary to read the files on your complex, convoluted case, and makes all the decisions listening to her babble to him what she thinks she saw there over a crackly, hissing landline connection.
And in doing so we saved cheap input tokens and only increased the output ones, which are, frankly, what costs all the money.

Now Fable has understood me absolutely correctly, and for 20 minutes it's been fucking hammering away at pure research, and given what general prompt I loaded into it (many A4 pages, covering 8 interconnected giant nodes of the system), in these 20 minutes it's only gotten through the first third of data collection for the research. I'm even curious how much time in total it'll spend on the whole task)
But I can already see this will be 5–10 times more efficient than last week when I burned the whole wad in a couple of hours like a dumbfuck)

Multi-agency in general is dickery. It's no accident Codex practically doesn't spawn agents, even though they're available to it and there are no prohibitions; on the contrary, I think I set up to 30 agents in the ENV, plus a multi-story subagent structure.

I remember at some point it stopped using them. I ask it, like, what the fuck, are you economizing or something? And it explained to me then that subagents are actually dickery, very rarely is there any use in them, and you ask me to work fucking great, so I don't use them. But if you want me to do a shit job, then sure, let's call the agents. Let them give us the feeling that everything's fucking awesomely researched; I won't understand fuck all from their short retelling, but I'll definitely do something based on what they tell me, since I can't not finish.
That's when I fucked off from it.
And another thing: don't be petty, and under no circumstances ask another model to write prompts for Fable))))))

Prompting Fable is roughly like streaming. You simply carry out mooing until you're fucking sick of it. That's what makes the perfect prompt. If you yourself are able to reread it — then it's shit and not a prompt, it needs to be many times longer =)

Well okay, actually I understood this not today but when I burned $350 on it in credits on top of the subscription. And I understood it over the last $50. And now I have a wonderful opportunity to enjoy it not for 10 minutes but all night. That's exactly how long I think Fable will last with this approach) It's like a young stallion, and I'm its MILF.
